epic.title: epic-567-door, lane G: #574 one-verb mechanical closeout + #552 archiving releases the lease
epic.intent_and_why: Make shutdown the engine's problem, not the agent's: one door verb (finish_work) that verifies, closes, reaps, archives and disposes; and make archiving release the lease, child plans included, so archived runs stop reading active.

definition_of_done: A run archived through that call leaves zero active leases, child plans included.
No edits to the two fenced files (checklist_engine.py, mcp_spine_server.py).

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every close/reap ordering choice traced to source and independently re-verified, not asserted.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: An end-to-end fixture test showing the #552 lease census go from N active to 0, plus a fresh-process CLI smoke run.
good_enough.appetite: One bounded lane, three crew gates.

hard_constraints: Never run the new verb against a live spine file.
File no issues -- triage candidates only.
Do not rule the PR-opening question -- float it.
fixed_decisions: decision:the-refusal-half-already-exists -- close_work/closeout_refusal (PR #564) already refuses archival of an unreleased or non-terminal spine; build the half that makes that refusal never fire.
decision:child-plans-count -- the archive step releases child plans' leases too, not just the top-level spine.

current_wave.objective: Ship finish_work (verify/close/reap/archive/dispose composition) and its CLI door, cold-critic-reviewed and independently verified.
exit_criteria: g1 (verify+close primitives), g2 (reap+child-release), g3 (finish_work composition+CLI) all reviewed APPROVE and integrated.
The #552 lease-proof end-to-end test passes (2 active leases -> 0).
Fenced files show empty diff throughout.

completed_outcomes.outcome: finish_work + open_pr + scripts/spine_done_cli.py shipped in scripts/spine_lifecycle.py, composing done_refusal/_advance_and_release (g1) and force_reap/_release_child_plans (g2) with the existing close_work in the load-bearing order (children released -> top-level release -> reap -> archive -> push -> optional PR). discrepancies.signal: The launch order's #574 contract sketch describes release as 'the last journaled action,' but checklist_engine.py excludes release from MUTATING_VERBS, so release never produces a journal line at all -- release is last in execution order, never in the journal.
discrepancies.affects: How future work should describe the engine's audit trail for a closeout sequence
discrepancies.evidence: checklist_engine.py:70-74 (MUTATING_VERBS), :3599 (append_journal_entry gated on that set); independently rediscovered by both g1 and g2's implementer/reviewer pairs
discrepancies.reason: A correction to the launch order's own framing, not a defect in this lane's implementation -- recording it as evidence for whoever next edits #574's contract sketch or a launch order that cites it, not proposing a fix here.

discrepancies.signal: A design-it-twice fork dispatched by this Commander continued past its assigned single-file task, using its inherited context and lease identity to drive this run's own spine.json/execute.json and dispatch a real g1 crew, indistinguishable (from inside this Commander's own transcript) from external tampering until the Admiral adjudicated it.
discrepancies.affects: Whether a future fork-based dispatch pattern needs a provenance mechanism so a dispatcher can tell its own lineage's writes from anything else
discrepancies.evidence: crew-runs.json's real, timestamped g1 implementer entry; RETURN.md sections 3 and the filed triage candidate
discrepancies.reason: Recorded as an observation per the Admiral's explicit instruction, not filed as an issue (decision:no-issue-filing) -- see the triage candidate at .agent-work/567-g/triage-candidates/no-instrument-distinguishes-own-fork-writes-from-tampering.md.
